channel.title: ExeBrowser — new games and posts
channel.description: Classic DOS and Windows games you can play free in your browser, plus write-ups on how the runtimes work.

item.title: New game: Chess
item.description: Stockfish 19 in your browser tab, turned down to whatever strength you want. Undo, flip the board, play either colour.

item.title: New game: Chess puzzles
item.description: Find the winning move. Thousands of real-game tactics, matched to your level, with a rating that follows you.

item.title: New game: Mahjong Solitaire
item.description: Clear the board by matching free tiles in pairs. Four layouts, hints, undo and a shuffle that never makes a game unwinnable.

item.title: New game: Checkers
item.description: American checkers with forced captures, multiple jumps and kings, against a computer at three strengths.

item.title: New game: Reversi
item.description: The disc-flipping strategy game on an 8×8 board, against a computer at three strengths.

item.title: New game: Four in a Row
item.description: Drop discs, line up four across, down or diagonally, and beat a computer that searches up to eight moves ahead.

item.title: New game: Backgammon
item.description: The two-thousand-year-old race game, with hits, the bar and gammons, against a computer opponent. Free, instant.

item.title: New game: NetHack
item.description: The official NetHack source compiled to WebAssembly. Pick a role, descend, save with S and come back later.

item.title: New game: Sudoku (Solo)
item.description: Play Sudoku free in your browser: endless generated puzzles from Trivial to Unreasonable, plus Jigsaw, Killer and X variants. Pencil marks and undo.

item.title: New game: Nonogram (Pattern)
item.description: Play nonograms free in your browser: shade the grid so each row and column matches its run lengths. Sizes from 10×10 to 30×30, new puzzle every time.

item.title: New game: Calcudoku (Keen)
item.description: Play Calcudoku free in your browser: fill a Latin square so each cage hits its sum, product, difference or quotient. 3×3 to 9×9, Easy to Unreasonable.

item.title: New game: Number loop puzzle (Loopy)
item.description: Play the number loop puzzle free in your browser: draw a single closed loop so each number has that many sides on it. Square, hexagon and Penrose grid

item.title: New game: Bridges puzzle (Bridges)
item.description: Play the Bridges puzzle free in your browser: link numbered islands with straight bridges so every island has its count and all are connected. 7×7 to

item.title: New game: Futoshiki (Unequal)
item.description: Play Futoshiki free in your browser: fill a Latin square that obeys every greater-than sign. 4×4 to 7×7, Easy to Extreme, plus the Adjacent variant.

item.title: New game: Skyscrapers (Towers)
item.description: Play Skyscrapers free in your browser: place towers of every height once per row and column so the edge clues count the towers visible. 4×4 to 9×9.

item.title: New game: Light Up puzzle (Light Up)
item.description: Play Light Up free in your browser: place bulbs so every white square is lit, no bulb shines on another, and numbered walls get their count. 7×7 to 14

item.title: How to Check if an .exe Is Safe Before You Run It
item.description: What you can learn about a Windows executable without running it — signature, publisher, imports, packing, entropy — what each thing is actually worth, and the limits of every method including scanners.

item.title: “A DLL Is Missing” — What It Means and How to Fix It
item.description: Why Windows says a program can't start because a DLL is missing, the four causes, why DLL download sites are the worst possible fix, and how to find out exactly which libraries a program needs.

item.title: How to Open an EXE File on Android, Honestly
item.description: Android cannot run Windows .exe files, and most guides promising otherwise are selling something. Here is what genuinely works in 2026 — a browser tab, Winlator, remote desktop — and where each one stops.

item.title: How to Open an EXE File on a Mac in 2026
item.description: Five honest ways to open a Windows .exe on a Mac — a browser tab with nothing installed, Wine, CrossOver, a virtual machine, or remote Windows — and what Apple Silicon changed about all of them.

item.title: What Is an .exe File — and How Do You Open One?
item.description: What a Windows .exe actually contains, how to open one on Windows, Mac, Linux, Chromebook and phones, how to look inside without running it, and when not to run it at all.

item.title: Why Won't My Old Program Run on Windows 11?
item.description: Six reasons old Windows software stops working on Windows 11 — missing 16-bit support, dead runtimes, broken installers, retired copy protection — and what actually fixes each one.

item.title: Open Cadet: Space Cadet Pinball, Fully Open Source
item.description: 3D Pinball Space Cadet needs a proprietary PINBALL.DAT to run. I rebuilt that data file from scratch — original art, 47 synthesized sounds, CC0 public domain — so the open-source engine finally runs with zero Microsoft files. Here's how.

item.title: How to Extract Files From an Installer, Without Installing
item.description: Old setup.exe won't run, but you just need the files inside? Here's how to unpack a legacy Windows installer — with 7-Zip, innoextract, cabextract, msiextract, or a browser sandbox — without a full install.

item.title: Where to Legally Get Classic Windows and DOS Games in 2026
item.description: An honest guide to legally free classic PC games in 2026: redistributable shareware, official freeware, open-source remakes, licensed storefronts — and the truth about abandonware.

item.title: Running 16-bit Windows 3.x Software in 2026
item.description: Why 16-bit Windows 3.x programs won't start on 64-bit Windows at all — and four honest ways to run them in 2026, including right in a browser tab.

item.title: We Tested 50+ Windows Apps in the Browser — What Runs
item.description: We ran more than 50 classic Windows and DOS programs through a browser-based Wine + DOSBox runtime and logged the results. Here's the full table: what plays instantly, what's partial, and what won't run.

item.title: How to Run Windows Software on a Chromebook (4 Ways)
item.description: Four realistic ways to run Windows programs on a Chromebook, ranked by effort: a no-install browser tool, Linux + Wine, remote desktop, and cloud Windows.

item.title: Wine vs. an Emulator: What's the Difference?
item.description: Wine is famously 'not an emulator' — what that means, how it differs from DOSBox-style emulation, and why running Windows apps in a browser needs both.

item.title: How to Run Old Windows Software Without a Virtual Machine
item.description: You don't always need a virtual machine to run an old Windows program. When a browser-based Wine tool is enough, when a VM is still the right call, and how to decide quickly.
